name: IceCube-Gen2: The Window to the Extreme Universe
notes: doc_type review_article is used because the enum has no “white paper” value; Part I of the Gen2 TDR is based on this document.

summary.plain: The science case for building a much bigger neutrino telescope at the South Pole, and what it would let astronomers see.
summary.technical: IceCube-Gen2 science white paper (J. Phys. G 48 (2021) 060501): design goals of resolving the TeV–EeV neutrino sky, multimessenger studies of cosmic particle acceleration, the origin of the highest-energy particles and fundamental-physics tests; ten times the cosmic-neutrino rate of IceCube, with a radio array extending the energy reach. Quotes an 8-year, ~$350M construction and full operation by 2033.
